answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce token stake before it can submit jobs, then slash that stake when independently sampled audits prove fabricated work or collusion. Honest agents recover the deposit and earn fees, while creating a swarm of disposable identities multiplies the capital tied up and the risk of losing it. A crystal-clear audit trail can distinguish useful nectar from spam, but the lotus of identities still costs the attacker real money and time to rebuild.
